text.p: Cash shortage caused by income tax payments pulled overnight money rates up sharply on Monday, but bond yields eased in mild buying amid expectations of an inflation-indexed bond auction for Tuesday, bankers said.

In line with the expectations, the Treasury announced a two-year, inflation-indexed risk premium bond auction with Wednesday value when 68 trillion lira of reverse repo deals will mature on the central bank's open market.
Bankers said today's National Security Council (MGK) meeting did not have much impact on the financial markets.

In order to relieve the cash demand, the central bank lent 14.1 trillion lira at 72 percent overnight at close and 33.7 trillion lira at 67 percent via tomorrow/next for expected cash shortage on Tuesday.
The average overnight money rate jumped to 71.79 percent from Friday's average of 55.05 percent. The average overnight repo rate also rose to 71.82 percent from 64.86 previous.
The yields on the bond market eased by around one percentage point, as demand for outstanding bonds rose after the Treasury announced an inflation-indexed bond auction for Tuesday, bankers said.
The most actively traded paper were April 29, 1998, yielding 97.22 percent, down 1.23 percentage point and December 10, 1997 at 91.39, down 0.94 percentage point from Friday.
Turkish lira weakened to 127,650 per dollar from 126,925 at Friday's close in line with the dollar mark parity.
